subject: earwig
title: A 10-Inch Worm Coils Inside a Half-Inch Earwig, Then Drowns It

scenes.text: Earwigs avoid open water. Some of them walk straight in.
Inside those earwigs is a coiled worm. In New Zealand, one measured over ten inches, in an insect barely half an inch long.
In 2019, scientists showed infected earwigs readily enter water, and the longer the worm, the more likely they go.
In 2026 they found part of how: thousands of genes change activity in the earwig and the worm at the same time.
When the worm is mature, its host heads for water, and the worm slides out.
The earwig dies there. It didn't fall in. It was steered.

description:
Some European earwigs carry a parasitic mermithid worm, Mermis nigrescens. Worms dissected from earwigs in Dunedin, New Zealand measured up to 263 mm, in an insect about 12 to 15 mm long.
A 2019 Parasitology study found infected earwigs readily enter water, with worm length a strong predictor; a 2026 Proc. R. Soc. B study found thousands of genes changing activity in both host and worm. The worm leaves the host in water and the earwig dies.
Which parasite creeps you out the most?
first_comment: Only adult worms made the earwigs go swimming. Have you ever found one of these worms in the garden?
